parts.title: NINE FIELDS
parts.intro_html:
a book about what reality is made of

and how to learn to feel it

chapters.title: Author's Note
chapters.html:
This book is an invitation to look at the world a little differently. We are used to thinking that reality simply exists: here is a table, here is time, here are the people around us. But if you look closely, it turns out that we also perceive all of this — and a great deal depends on exactly how we do it.

I will tell you about nine fields. A field is not a place or a bodily organ. It is a way in which life unfolds before us, and at the same time the way in which we notice it. One field is responsible for order and structure, another for infinite space, a third for time, a fourth for growth, and so on. Together they form a single picture — from the most solid and shaped to the most whole and boundless.

I have tried to write simply. No special preparation is needed here — only curiosity and the wish to understand yourself and the world a little more deeply. Each chapter can be read on its own, but it is better to read them in order: that way the nine fields gradually come together into one living system. Let us set out.

chapters.title: Chapter One. What a Field Is — and Why There Are Nine
chapters.html:
Imagine you are looking at one and the same garden through different windows. From one you see neat beds and paths — order. From another, the boundless sky above the garden. From a third you notice how everything grows and changes. The garden is one, but each window shows its own truth. Fields are just such windows of perception. There are nine of them, and each shows the world in its own way.

The nine fields are not arranged by chance. They run from the most dense and shaped to the most whole and all-encompassing. First — structure, the skeleton of things. Then space, time, growth. Then the way we look at the world from the outside: our attention, movement, connections, boundaries. And finally the whole, in which all the fields become mere facets of one.

Three states: seed, sprout, tree

Each field has three states, and this is perhaps the most important thing to remember. Let us call the first state MA — this is potential. Imagine a seed: a whole tree is already hidden within it, but it cannot yet be seen. The second state — ZHI — is when the tree has already grown and stands before you; you can touch it. And between them there is a transition, the moment of sprouting — it is called KUN.

Everything in the world travels this path: first a hidden possibility, then sprouting, then a finished form. A child is born with an inbuilt code — and gradually unfolds. An intention lives in the mind — and one day becomes a deed. A chair was first an idea, and now you can sit on it. Wherever we look, we see either a seed, or a sprout, or a tree.

Seed — sprout — tree. Everything travels this path.

These same three states explain where difficulties come from. When force gets stuck in the seed and cannot sprout, stagnation sets in and everything freezes inside. When force bursts outward too violently, without measure, destruction begins. And when the very link between intention and deed is lost, a person tries hard but everything comes to nothing. We will speak of these shadows in every chapter — not to frighten, but so as to recognize them in time.

chapters.title: Chapter Two. LOGOS — the Field of Structure
chapters.html:
Logos is the skeleton of the world. Everything around us rests on something: a house has a frame, a story has cause and effect, music has rhythm and rules. Logos is that invisible load-bearing structure, the order on which the rest stands.

Logos answers the question “how is this arranged?” This field loves clarity, sequence, a reliable support. If we imagine reality as a book, then Logos is its grammar: without it the words fall apart, and with it they add up into meaning.

One might say that Logos is code. The seed already records what the tree will grow into; the intention already conceals the future thing. When the time comes, the code unfolds — and we see the finished form. Energy in this field flows from top to bottom, down steps, where each rests on the previous one, and finally grounds itself in the feet.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Logos first of all sets things in order. They turn chaos into lists and diagrams, look for the guiding principle, think honestly — “if this, then that” — and know how to bring dreams down into concrete plans. It is calm beside them: there is something to lean on.

The shadow of the field

But order has its reverse side too. Sometimes structure ossifies — rules are followed simply because that is how it has always been, even when they already get in the way. And sometimes a person begins to impose their order on everyone around them, and then rules turn into a cage. A healthy Logos is alive: it holds form but does not stifle.

« Logos is the skeleton, but the skeleton must serve the living body, not the other way round. »

chapters.title: Chapter Three. NIMA — the Field of Space
chapters.html:
If Logos is the skeleton, then Nima is the openness in which everything fits. Imagine a clear sky or a boundless field: nothing has been built there yet, but for that very reason everything is possible there. Nima is space and the infinite freedom of possibilities.

The most astonishing thing about this field is that it has no walls and no rules. It simply is. All the boundaries we feel are in fact drawn by our own mind — which means they can be pushed back. There is room for everything: space does not run out and can contain any structure.

In Nima the past, present and future lie side by side, in a single moment. This is the field of possibilities: from here we can change our life, because we see not a single road but many. Energy here radiates from the center in even rays, like sunlight, and just as calmly gathers back again.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Nima is not afraid of the unknown. They hold several options in mind at once and are in no hurry to grab the first. They know how to change a heavy situation simply by looking at it more broadly, and they easily master the new — be it places, ideas or whole worlds.

The shadow of the field

The shadow of this field is to get lost in infinity. When there are too many possibilities, one may never choose any and freeze in daydreams. Or, on the contrary, one may let in chaos, in which everything mixes together and there is nothing to lean on. A healthy Nima gives openness but remembers that sooner or later something must be chosen from the possibilities.

« There is always enough space. Only our thoughts get cramped. »

chapters.title: Chapter Four. ANDRA — the Field of Connection and Time
chapters.html:
Andra is attraction. Here time appears for the first time, and it is experienced in an unusual way — as a pull. It is as if something draws us forward, toward what we are yet to become. And this is quite unlike the measured ticking of a clock.

Imagine a great tree. It seems already to exist in the future — and it pulls toward itself the little seed from which it will grow. So too with us: the future draws us to itself. We feel that we are being led somewhere, that certain deeds we somehow cannot do, while toward something else we are drawn irresistibly.

Andra is also love as action, joining and parting. Everything we have lived through is, as it were, recorded in our “seed” and then determines which life we will be drawn to next. Energy here coils in a soft spiral inward, joining — and if something must be let go, the spiral unwinds back again.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Andra is the very “glue” between people. They reconcile, unite, create a warm atmosphere in which others want to move toward one another. They finely sense both their own body and another's state, and know how to bring to a close in good time what has outlived itself, without strain.

The shadow of the field

The shadow comes from two sides. One may dissolve so completely into another person that one ceases to be oneself — this is merging. Or, fearing pain, one may sever connections before they even arise. A healthy Andra knows how both to join and to remain oneself.

« The future does not wait ahead of us — it quietly draws us to itself even now. »

chapters.title: Chapter Five. ZINGRA — the Field of Transformation
chapters.html:
Zingra is growth and transformation. If Andra pulls us toward the future, then Zingra is the very work of transformation that goes on inside us without cease. It is the fire that makes the seed sprout.

What is laid within us does not lie idle — it is constantly sprouting. As soon as you set yourself an image to strive toward, it begins to grow, as if wings were breaking through. Zingra brings outward what was hidden within, and each new turn raises us a little higher.

This is the field of zeal and the thirst for life. Energy here unwinds in a spiral outward, hot and striving upward, like a flame. It is Zingra that turns a vague desire into a clear goal, and a goal into movement.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Zingra cannot stand still. Having reached one thing, they are already looking at the next summit. They turn desires into deeds, infect others with their fire, and meet any difficulty as an occasion to grow.

The shadow of the field

But fire can also be treacherous. Sometimes growth is only pretended: a person acts as if they are developing, but in fact marks time. And sometimes, on the contrary, they chase change so greedily that they fail to live through any of it. A healthy Zingra grows but lets the fruit ripen.

« Set yourself an image — and it will begin to grow. That is how wings break through. »

chapters.title: Chapter Six. LUBA — the Field of the Center
chapters.html:
Luba is the center, the core, the point of “here and now.” Everything in the world has a core, and if you shift it, the whole picture changes. This is the field of our attention and, most importantly, of our freedom to choose.

Our attention is not a passive spectator. It is able to change the course of events, to hasten change, to choose the road. Look at how a tree grows: meeting a stone, it does not batter against it but calmly goes around and still reaches upward. So too we are free to choose where to direct our life.

This is what free will consists of. The key is always in our hands. Energy here does not spread out but gathers into a single point — like the flame of a candle: still, quiet, yet lighting all around.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Luba becomes a center by their very being. When they enter and begin to speak, they are listened to. They lean on an inner “I am” that does not depend on others' judgments, achieve their aim not by pressure but by calm strength, and know how to gather the most varied people around a common idea.

The shadow of the field

The shadow is either to lose one's center and fall apart, chasing after support from outside, or to turn oneself into the center of the universe, which only demands and gives nothing. A healthy Luba shines rather than scorches.

« The key is always in your hands. Attention chooses where to grow. »

chapters.title: Chapter Seven. TUMA — the Field of Movement
chapters.html:
Tuma is movement itself, time felt from within. If Andra pulled us into the future, then Tuma is the experiencing of the path itself, the sense that we are moving from one point to another.

Imagine that a sprout suddenly became aware that it is growing — that is Tuma. It is the living feeling of the flow of time. And the most interesting thing: this feeling can be governed. We can, as it were, slow time down, change how we live a moment, appraise an event differently.

True, Tuma has a limit: it is mistress of the moment but not of the outcome. It can change how you pass along the path, but not what your “tree” will finally grow into. Energy here moves in waves, like a pulse, threading events one onto another into an even stream.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Tuma ends up in the right place at the right time as if without effort. They trust the flow of life, do not try to clutch at every trifle, and know how to live a moment whole — without getting stuck in the past or worrying about the future.

The shadow of the field

The shadow is either to freeze, to fall out of time, watching life pass by, or to race on without stopping, failing to truly live through anything. A healthy Tuma flows evenly: neither standing still nor fussing.

« You can slow your own time. You can change the path — but not necessarily the outcome. »

chapters.title: Chapter Eight. ASTRA — the Field of Connections and Paths
chapters.html:
Astra is all the roads and connections of the world. If Nima is pure space, where nothing has yet been laid, then Astra is the same space, but already inhabited: with paths, channels, bridges between people and worlds.

Wherever our attention has once passed, a trace remains — like a path on the grass. Over time such paths grow more numerous, weaving into a whole network of ways. Astra is the space where someone has already been, where something has already happened.

This is the field of communication and the word. Energy here works like a pump: an in-breath — we receive; an out-breath — we give. So a living exchange is born: connections stretch out, words fly, thoughts find one another.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Astra knows how to explain the complex in simple words so that everyone understands. They feel the rhythm of a conversation — when to listen, when to answer — easily connect people who did not know one another before, and hear even what has been left unsaid.

The shadow of the field

The shadow comes in extremes. On one side — loneliness, when connections are severed and words find no addressee. On the other — noise, when there are so many words that they lose their weight. A healthy Astra values a clean, honest exchange.

« Where attention once passed, a path remains. That is how ways are born. »

chapters.title: Chapter Nine. BITRA — the Field of Boundaries
chapters.html:
Bitra is boundary and form. For something to exist, it must have an edge: a drop has a surface, a house has walls, we ourselves have a sense of where “I” end. Bitra outlines space and holds form.

Our perception is arranged in an interesting way: out of boundless openness it singles out a center and edges. Toward the center everything grows denser — one can go deeper endlessly, like digging into the earth. Toward the edges, on the contrary, it thins out and recedes into vast distances. And this center is we ourselves, our perception.

But there are many centers: there is I, there is my family, my people, the planet, and something greater still above them. And here is what matters: by changing our awareness, we rebuild the whole picture. The world depends on how we look at it — which means one can travel along its roads. Energy here moves in a circle, keeping form and not letting attention spread out.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Bitra knows how to say “no” gently but firmly and not torment themselves with guilt. They hold attention on one matter for a long time, bring what they have begun to a finished form, and create around themselves a sense of safety — for beside them the rules are clear.

The shadow of the field

The shadow is either to lock oneself in too thick a shell, which cannot be broken through even from within, or to lose one's boundaries entirely, spreading out and unable to protect oneself. A healthy Bitra is a flexible boundary: it keeps but does not imprison.

« The world depends on how we look. By changing our gaze, we change the world. »

chapters.title: Chapter Ten. OMA — the Field of Wholeness
chapters.html:
Oma is the whole. All eight fields we have spoken of enter into it, like facets of a single gem. Here everything is present at once: strict order and its absence, structure and infinite freedom.

Oma gathers everything into one. One field determines what we are attuned to; another unfolds what is laid within; in space much is simply foreordained. And there is a subtle but important thought: space itself is empty, it has no structure. We live within space, but we live by the laws of structure — and so a whole world arises around us. As soon as order enters space, life begins.

In this field the mystery of time is also revealed. Energy here flows in all directions at once, taking in all movements — spirals, waves, rays and circles. When Oma awakens, the flow rises along the spine and threads through all the fields at once, joining them into one.

When the field is open

A person with a strong Oma sees the whole picture, without dividing the world into black and white. They calmly contain opposites, feel themselves part of a great world, and have no discord between what they think, say and do. Beside them life seems to grow brighter.

The shadow of the field

The shadow is either to dissolve into “all this” and lose oneself, or to decide that one has already attained everything and understood everything — which is only a beautiful self-deception. A healthy Oma is a unity in which neither you nor others are lost.

« As soon as order enters space — life begins. »

chapters.title: Chapter Eleven. Time That Can Be Stopped — the Mystery of the Pause
chapters.html:
We are used to thinking that time always goes on and cannot be stopped. But in the world of fields things are a little different. The code of the future may lie in the seed and wait — for as long as needed — until the time comes to wake it. Time in this sense does not flow constantly: it switches on when it is needed.

Recall the tree that draws the seed toward itself. While time goes on, the seed grows toward the tree. But if time is removed, everything freezes in wait for the right moment — like a stilled youth that is in no hurry anywhere.

From this a beautiful possibility for inner work is born. One can attune to other versions of oneself, change fields, stretch and slow one's own time. One part of our world can stand on pause while another goes on living and moving.

Time switches on upon request. In the pause it is as if it were absent — and yet it is there.

chapters.title: Chapter Twelve. Fields at Your Fingertips — Working with the Hands
chapters.html:
Fields can be worked with the hands, not only the mind. The palms have long been folded into particular gestures — and not without reason. The left hand is closer to the hidden, to what is still ripening within; the right — to what has already manifested and lives.

The lower row of fields

Four fingers are the first four fields. They are counted from the little finger to the index finger, the same on both hands: the little finger — the first field, the ring finger — the second, the middle — the third, the index — the fourth. The hand grows used to this quickly.

The upper row of fields

And then the most interesting part begins. The thumb here works as a switch. While it is held aside, the four fingers stand for the first fields. But lower it and press it to the palm — and the same fingers sound differently: now they give the fields from the fifth to the eighth. It is like a musical instrument: the keys are the same, but change the register — and the melody is quite different. The count here goes from the little finger in the reverse direction: eight, seven, six, five.

How to do it

It is most convenient to work at the level of the solar plexus — where the sense of force lives. Feel how energy flows through the fingers and out into infinity. The thumb is pressed firmly to the center of the palm. Do not hurry: the body needs time to remember these gestures and fill them with living feeling.

chapters.title: Final Chapter. In Place of an Afterword
chapters.html:
We have passed through the nine fields — from the solid skeleton of Logos to the boundless wholeness of Oma. Along the way we met space and time, growth and attention, movement, connections and boundaries. And at the very end all of this gathered into one.

There is no need to memorize the nine fields as a list. Far more valuable is to begin to notice them. In your own mood, in a conversation with a loved one, in the way you make a decision or live through an ordinary day. The fields are not somewhere far off: they are right here, in every breath and glance of ours.

May this book become not a code of rules but your companion — a reference to return to at the right moment. Look into any chapter when you feel that some field is asking for attention. Life itself will suggest the rest.

If you wish to dig deeper, turn to the practicing masters of the DARs: they will suggest where to begin and will help you make sense of the subtleties.

chapters.title: Appendix. The Map of DARs
chapters.html: The complete map of the combinations of the nine fields in two positions — MA (potential) and ZHI (manifestation). Each cell is its own DAR with its own name and sign.
